Right skew is defined at 68-84 ('right hand side of this particular curve is little bit elongated'), symmetric at 217-230 ('the right hand curve will almost be equal to the left hand curve... mirror'), and left/negative skew at 233-240. The ordering rule (mean > median > mode for right skew, the reverse for negative skew) is asserted at 291-353 'just by seeing this particular diagram'. It is never explained, and nothing says the mean is pulled by extreme values. The wealth example (99-127) is used only to illustrate the shape, not the mean. So f3 is not taught; f1 and f2 are. The other ~3 of the 5 minutes are padding: a second comment-length example (127-170), references to 'the morning video' and 'my channel' (25-54, 160-170, 277-280), and a machine-learning aside (178-217: iris dataset, 'most of the machine learning algorithm likes the data to have this kind of normal distribution'). The clip also states 'symmetrical distribution... this is nothing but our normal distribution' (171-176), which wrongly treats symmetric and normal as the same thing. The lifespan example for left skew (249-275) is muddled: it says both early deaths and people living past 70 are rare. No contiguous cut keeps all three shapes without the tangents, so this is ~5 min for ~90 s of teaching. The video also has the visual mode wrong: it is Krish Naik drawing curves on a whiteboard, not diagram_animation.
